Vision-language models (VLMs) have become a common foundation for vision-and-language navigation in continuous environments (VLN-CE).Yet most VLM-based methods cast navigation as low-level action prediction, an interface that is ambiguous, tied to short-horizon motion primitives, and inefficient due to repeated VLM querying.

We propose Goal2Pixel, a pure pixel-based paradigm that reformulates VLN-CE as navigable pixel grounding. Rather than predicting actions, Goal2Pixel uses the image plane as a unified spatial interface between VLM reasoning and robot motion: the model predicts a visible navigable pixel, which is back-projected into a 3D waypoint for forward navigation.

Non-forward actions are encoded by auxiliary left/right/bottom regions for turning and stopping. To support long-horizon navigation, we propose ViKeyMem, a visibility-aware keyframe memory, achieving a favorable performance-efficiency trade-off while reducing training cost by over 50%.

To adapt pretrained VLMs to navigable pixel grounding, we introduce semantic embeddings and coordinate-aware auxiliary losses. Among methods trained without external data, Goal2Pixel achieves competitive state-of-the-art performance on R2R-CE and RxR-CE. On R2R-CE Val-Unseen, it achieves 54.1% SR and 52.5% SPL with only 7.75 VLM calls per episode.

Compared with direct action prediction, Goal2Pixel improves SR by 21.2 percentage points while requiring 6 times fewer VLM calls. Project Page: https://baobao0926.github.io/Goal2Pixel/.

summary.en: The paper proposes Goal2Pixel, which frames vision-language navigation in continuous environments as navigable-pixel grounding. The model predicts a visible target pixel in an image, which is back-projected into a 3D waypoint; auxiliary image regions encode turning and stopping. For long-horizon navigation, the authors introduce visibility-aware keyframe memory, ViKeyMem, reporting a favorable performance-efficiency trade-off and over 50% lower training cost. Among methods trained without external data, Goal2Pixel reports competitive state-of-the-art results on R2R-CE and RxR-CE, including 54.1% success and 52.5% SPL on R2R-CE Val-Unseen.
summary.zh: 论文提出 Goal2Pixel，将连续环境中的视觉语言导航表述为可导航像素定位：模型在图像中预测一个可见目标像素，再将其反投影为三维航点；转向和停止则由辅助图像区域编码。为支持长程导航，作者提出可见性感知关键帧记忆 ViKeyMem，并报告其在性能与效率间取得较好平衡、训练成本降低超过50%。在不使用外部数据训练的方法中，Goal2Pixel 在 R2R-CE 和 RxR-CE 上达到有竞争力的最先进表现；在 R2R-CE Val-Unseen 上，成功率为54.1%，SPL为52.5%，每回合调用视觉语言模型7.75次。

items.title: Goal2Pixel: Grounding Goals to Pixels for Vision-Language Navigation

sections.text:
Robot policy evaluation often relies on a binary success signal for task completion. In real-world deployment, however, desired execution behaviors are also defined by quality attributes such as execution speed and motion smoothness, which need to be dynamically controlled according to task requirements.

To address this, we introduce Quality-Controllable Policy (QCP), a robot policy that enables inference-time control over both individual quality attributes and their combinations.

To extend the controllable quality range beyond initial demonstrations, we further propose an iterative hindsight relabeling loop: QCP collects online rollouts under target quality labels, adds successful trajectories to the dataset, relabels the accumulated trajectories in hindsight according to their measured quality, and fine-tunes the policy.

Experiments on Robomimic and RoboEval demonstrate that QCP consistently improves both task execution quality and success rates across iterations, producing successful rollouts that exceed the quality of the initial demonstrations.

Finally, we validate QCP on real-world manipulation tasks, where controlling speed increases throughput in conveyor operations and controlling transport stability improves success when carrying wine glasses, demonstrating that quality-controllable policies yield practical gains in physical deployment.

summary.en: The paper introduces Quality-Controllable Policy (QCP), which controls individual execution qualities, such as speed and smoothness, and their combinations at inference time. An iterative hindsight relabeling loop collects successful rollouts under target quality labels, relabels trajectories by measured quality, and fine-tunes the policy. In Robomimic and RoboEval experiments, the authors report improvements in execution quality and success across iterations. Real-world manipulation tests report higher conveyor throughput through speed control and better success carrying wine glasses through stability control.
summary.zh: 论文提出质量可控策略 QCP，使机器人在推理时能够控制执行速度、运动平滑度等单项质量属性及其组合。为扩展示范数据覆盖的质量范围，方法通过迭代式事后重标记收集目标质量下的在线成功轨迹，按实测质量重新标记累积数据并微调策略。在 Robomimic 和 RoboEval 实验中，作者报告多轮迭代提升了执行质量与成功率，生成轨迹质量超过初始示范。真实操作任务中，速度控制提高了传送带作业吞吐量，运输稳定性控制改善了携带酒杯时的成功表现。

items.title: Learning Quality-Controllable Robot Policies with Iterative Hindsight Relabeling

sections.text:
Natural language interaction provides an intuitive way for non-expert users to communicate with robotic platforms. However, transforming user requests into executable navigation actions remains a challenging task, requiring the integration of language understanding, environment perception, and autonomous navigation.

This work presents a language-driven navigation framework that enables mobile robots to interpret user requests in natural language to move the robot to a destination and autonomously navigate towards it. The framework is composed of modular ROS 2 components that cooperate to transform natural language instructions into navigation actions.

Given a natural language request referring to a target in the environment (e.g., "go to the mail box"), the system identifies the referenced object, estimates its position using RGB-D data, and generates a navigation goal, which is then executed through the ROS 2 Nav2 navigation stack.

The ROS 2-based implementation facilitates portability across different robotic platforms, requiring only the configuration of the corresponding topics and services. The system is evaluated in both simulation and real-world scenarios using a TurtleBot3 Waffle and a Unitree Go2 robot with a RealSense camera.

Experimental results show that the framework successfully interprets both direct commands and contextual requests, generates meaningful natural-language feedback, and navigates towards the desired target.

These results demonstrate the feasibility of combining semantic perception and autonomous navigation to provide an intuitive human-robot interaction paradigm. Code will be released as open source upon acceptance.

summary.en: The paper presents a vision-language navigation framework that converts natural-language requests into goals for mobile robots. It identifies the referenced object, estimates its position from RGB-D data, and executes navigation through ROS 2 Nav2. The modular ROS 2 implementation is described as portable across platforms through configuration of topics and services. The system was evaluated in simulation and real-world scenarios using TurtleBot3 Waffle and Unitree Go2 robots with a RealSense camera. The authors report successful interpretation, feedback, and navigation toward targets.
summary.zh: 论文提出一种基于视觉语言与 RGB-D 感知的移动机器人语义导航框架，将自然语言请求转换为导航目标。系统识别请求所指物体，利用 RGB-D 数据估计其位置，再通过 ROS 2 Nav2 执行导航；模块化 ROS 2 实现可通过配置主题和服务适配不同平台。作者使用配备 RealSense 相机的 TurtleBot3 Waffle 和 Unitree Go2，在仿真与真实场景中评估系统。实验结果显示，系统能够处理直接命令和上下文请求、生成自然语言反馈，并导航至目标。

items.title: From Language to Navigation Goals: A Vision-Language Approach for Semantic Navigation of Mobile Robots Using RGB-D Perception

sections.text:
World-action models (WAMs) offer a promising framework for embodied intelligence, yet mainstream approaches remain centered on video foundation models or vision-language models.

Even when geometric features extracted by 3D models such as VGGT are incorporated, they are typically passed into a video model or VLM that serves as the primary backbone, leaving 3D geometry as an auxiliary input or prediction target rather than the native foundation for world modeling.

We present E0.5, a geometry-native world-action model built directly on 3D foundation models. E0.5 introduces two key innovations. First, it adopts a 3D foundation model as the primary backbone, making 3D geometry the native representation for both world modeling and action prediction.

Second, it explicitly predicts future 3D states together with actions, enabling the model to capture geometric world dynamics beyond action-only modeling or future video prediction.

Experiments on RoboTwin 2.0 first demonstrate the effectiveness of E0.5 without embodied-data pretraining, achieving success rates of 89.90\% and 50.09\% under clean and randomized settings, respectively.

Building on these results, we further pretrain E0.5 on more than 160k robot trajectories from AgiBotWorld-Beta, jointly learning robot actions and future geometry within the pretrained 3D foundation.

This embodied pretraining improves mean real-world manipulation success rates by approximately 15 and 7 percentage points on AgileX Piper and Zerith H1, respectively. Together, these results demonstrate the potential of geometry-native foundations to acquire robot interaction knowledge and transfer it to physical manipulation.

E0.5 embodies this geometry-native approach as a member of the VWA family of world-action models.

summary.en: The paper introduces E0.5, a geometry-native world-action model built on a 3D foundation model. It uses 3D geometry as the basis for world modeling and action prediction, and predicts future 3D states jointly with actions. On RoboTwin 2.0, E0.5 without embodied-data pretraining achieves the reported success rates in clean and randomized settings. After pretraining on robot trajectories from AgiBotWorld-Beta, real-world manipulation experiments on AgileX Piper and Zerith H1 show mean success-rate gains of approximately 15 and 7 percentage points, respectively. The authors describe this as evidence of transfer potential.
summary.zh: 论文提出 E0.5，一种以三维基础模型为主干的几何原生世界动作模型，将三维几何作为世界建模和动作预测的基础表示，并联合预测未来三维状态与动作。在 RoboTwin 2.0 上，未使用具身数据预训练的 E0.5 在干净和随机化设置下取得摘要所报成功率。随后，作者用 AgiBotWorld-Beta 的机器人轨迹进行预训练；在 AgileX Piper 与 Zerith H1 的真实操作实验中，平均成功率分别提高约 15 和 7 个百分点。作者据此指出，该方法展现了几何原生基础模型学习交互知识并迁移至实体操作的潜力。

items.title: E0.5: From Reconstructive to Future-Predictive 3D Foundations for Robotic World-Action Modeling

sections.text:
Medium altitude, long endurance unmanned aerial systems such as Shahed-type strike drones are an unanswered threat in modern conflicts. Conventional air defense systems are too expensive to provide a feasible large-scale solution.

Quadcopter interceptors are a cheap, battle-proven alternative, but their extremely limited flight time restricts them to low altitude targets at short range, whereas fixed-wing platforms have the endurance to reach higher altitude targets from longer distances. However, such interceptors are still operated manually.

Recent developments in learning-based controllers show potential for automation. In this work, a fixed-wing interceptor is presented that is controlled by a neural network that maps filtered monocular vision observations directly to actuator commands.

The policy was trained in a custom Python environment using reinforcement learning and proximal policy optimization. The policy was then deployed on a fixed-wing platform and tested in real interception scenarios. As a baseline, two classical guidance controllers were also developed and tested in simulation.

The policy is able to intercept targets both in simulation and in real flight. In simulation, the policy outperforms the classical controllers under most conditions. The interceptor was ultimately successfully validated in real flight by intercepting maneuvering fixed-wing targets.

This novel system shows the potential of artificial intelligence for autonomous control of fixed-wing interceptor drones.

summary.en: The paper presents a fixed-wing interceptor controlled by a neural network that maps filtered monocular-vision observations directly to actuator commands. The policy was trained with proximal policy optimization in a custom Python environment, deployed on a fixed-wing platform, and tested in real interceptions. Two classical guidance controllers served as simulation baselines. The authors report that the learned policy intercepted targets in simulation and real flight, outperformed the baselines in simulation under most conditions, and successfully intercepted maneuvering fixed-wing targets in real flight.
summary.zh: 本文提出一种固定翼拦截无人机控制方法，用神经网络将经过滤波的单目视觉观测直接映射为执行器指令。策略在自建 Python 环境中通过近端策略优化训练，并部署到固定翼平台；作者还在仿真中测试了两种经典制导控制器作为基线。仿真结果显示，该策略在多数条件下优于基线；仿真和真实飞行中均实现拦截，并在真实飞行中成功拦截了机动固定翼目标。

items.title: Autonomous fixed-wing interception using reinforcement learning

sections.text:
World Action Models (WAMs) combine future-video prediction with robot action learning, yet improvements in task success alone do not reveal how predictive supervision manifests in execution behavior or whether its benefits persist under task and environmental shifts.

We conduct controlled future-video prediction loss ablations within FastWAM and OpenWAM, keeping model architecture, initialization, robot training data, and training steps fixed within each model family. Under clean conditions on seen tasks, predictive supervision increases success rates by 24.38 and 72.91 percentage points, respectively.

Trajectory clustering further reveals higher success rates within several coarse trajectory clusters, including cases where cluster frequencies change little, indicating that the gains are not solely reflected in changes in the prevalence of trajectory patterns.

However, these benefits do not consistently persist under distribution shifts: improvements on unseen tasks vary across models and tasks, while both models exhibit low success rates under the evaluated environmental randomizations, without a consistent advantage from predictive supervision.

We further introduce future-video prediction as an auxiliary training objective for $\pi_{0.5}$, where a lightweight Transformer predictor used only during training increases success from 82.94% to 89.19%.

These findings support future-video prediction as effective auxiliary supervision for action learning, while distinguishing improved execution on familiar tasks from reliable transfer and showing that such gains need not rely on a large pretrained video diffusion transformer (DiT) in the evaluated setting.

summary.en: The authors conduct controlled future-video prediction loss ablations in FastWAM and OpenWAM, holding architecture, initialization, robot training data, and training steps fixed within each model family. Predictive supervision raises success on seen tasks under clean conditions, and trajectory clustering shows gains within several coarse clusters. Transfer is inconsistent: results on unseen tasks vary by model and task, while both models have low success under the evaluated environmental randomizations without a consistent advantage. An auxiliary prediction objective for π₀.₅ also increases success in the reported evaluation.
summary.zh: 本文通过受控消融研究未来视频预测监督对机器人动作学习的作用，在 FastWAM 和 OpenWAM 各自模型系列内固定架构、初始化、机器人训练数据和训练步数。已见任务的干净条件下，预测监督提高了成功率；轨迹聚类也显示若干类别内成功率上升。作者指出，这些收益在分布变化下并不稳定：未见任务结果因模型和任务而异，环境随机化下两模型成功率均低，且没有一致优势。对 π₀.₅ 的辅助训练实验也报告成功率提升。

items.title: What Does World Modeling Actually Improve in Robot Action Learning?

sections.text:
Handheld data-collection interfaces such as the Universal Manipulation Interface (UMI) allow manipulation demonstrations to be gathered in the wild without a robot in the loop, but the quality of the resulting action labels is bounded by the accuracy of vision-based localization.

Existing systems recover end-effector pose from monocular visual-inertial odometry, which is subject to scale ambiguity and drift, or delegate tracking to closed-source modules and external infrastructure that reintroduce cost and setup burden.

We present OpenJaws, a fully open hardware and software framework for sensorized UMI that improves localization and simplifies deployment across robot platforms. OpenJaws pairs a modular, 3D-printed gripper exposing a standardized ISO adapter with a low-cost stereo camera to recover metric camera trajectories.

We further introduce UMI-Loc-Bench-v1, a benchmark quantifying real-world localization accuracy for handheld data-collection devices, and show that stereo localization substantially outperforms monocular alternatives. Finally, we demonstrate that policies trained on data collected with OpenJaws can be deployed on a real robot across multiple tasks.

Hardware, software, and data are released under a commercially permissive license. Code, data, and videos are available at https://open-jaws.github.io/

summary.en: OpenJaws is an open hardware and software framework for collecting manipulation demonstrations with a sensorized Universal Manipulation Interface. It combines a modular 3D-printed gripper with a standardized ISO adapter and a low-cost stereo camera to recover metric camera trajectories. The authors introduce UMI-Loc-Bench-v1 to quantify real-world localization accuracy for handheld data-collection devices, and report that stereo localization substantially outperforms monocular alternatives. They also demonstrate deployment on a real robot across multiple tasks for policies trained with OpenJaws-collected data.
summary.zh: 本文介绍 OpenJaws，一个用于通用操作数据采集的开放硬件与软件 UMI 框架。它将模块化 3D 打印夹爪、标准化 ISO 接口与低成本双目相机结合，以恢复具有尺度的相机轨迹。作者还提出 UMI-Loc-Bench-v1，用于评估手持采集设备在真实环境中的定位精度，并报告双目定位显著优于单目替代方案。使用 OpenJaws 采集的数据训练出的策略已在真实机器人上跨多个任务部署。

items.title: OpenJaws: An Open Hardware UMI Framework with Stereo Localization for Generalist Manipulation

sections.text:
As robotic systems grow more general, legal norms are needed to integrate them into society.

This paper extends the isomorphism problem of aligning legal source texts with their encodings, and measures two key challenges to robot normative control: （1） the grounding isomorphism gap, where perception error grounds false atoms for legal reasoning, and （2） the ontological isomorphism gap, where one legal conclusion admits many faithful translations into planning constraints.

The paper introduces a legal planning stack that employs Defeasible Deontic Logic (DDL) to constrain a motion planner. The stack leverages learned world models to plan and to provide legal context, enabling ex ante governance that intervenes before an illegal action is executed. It was deployed on a simulated robot arm pushing a cube across a 3x3 grid.

The findings were （1） the legislated agent abided substantially more often than the non-legislated one, and modeling perception uncertainty lifted abidance even further, （2） the legal reasoning ran efficiently at runtime and its verdicts were auditable, and （3） the stack adapted to exogenous signals and endogenous rule changes.

Both gaps were measured: （4） world model and probe error corrupted the factual input for the DDL reasoner, and （5） a single law admitted several faithful metric interpretations yielding drastically different abidance.

Thus, ex ante legislation functions as intended, and closing these gaps with a standardized mapping from the law to runtime constraints and improved fact grounding from perception will yield robust laws that align robot behavior with society's norms. Project page: https://dylanwaldner-cail.github.io/Legislated-Planner/.

summary.en: The paper presents a legal planning stack that uses Defeasible Deontic Logic to constrain a motion planner, with learned world models supporting planning and legal context. It was evaluated on a simulated robot arm pushing a cube across a grid. The authors report that the legislated agent abided more often than the non-legislated agent, with further improvement when perception uncertainty was modeled. Legal reasoning was efficient at runtime and auditable, and the stack adapted to external signals and rule changes. The evaluation also found that perception errors and alternative faithful mappings of a law to planning constraints affected abidance.
summary.zh: 本文提出一个将法律推理接入机器人运动规划的规划栈，使用可废止义务逻辑约束规划器，并借助学习到的世界模型提供规划与法律情境。该系统在模拟机械臂推动方格网立方体的任务中评估。作者报告，受法律约束的智能体更常遵守规则，纳入感知不确定性后遵守率进一步提高；推理运行高效且可审计，也能适应外部信号和规则变化。实验还揭示感知事实错误及同一法律的不同规划约束映射会影响遵守情况。

items.title: Legislating World-Model-Based Planning with Legal Reasoning

sections.text:
Action-conditioned world models offer a scalable alternative to costly real-world interaction for improving robot policies.

However, existing world-model-based methods largely treat world models as forward-only surrogates of the physical environment, leaving untapped a capability no physical environment affords: rewinding to past decision points to explore counterfactual futures.

We introduce Rollback, a policy improvement paradigm that turns world models from passive simulators into counterfactual engines: it rolls back to critical decision points, branches into alternative actions, and contrasts their outcomes to attribute success to individual decisions.

This concentrates imagination where it matters most and distills counterfactual outcomes into fine-grained, action-level supervision without a separately learned value model.

We build a scalable training system that unifies distributed world-model search with asynchronous real-robot execution, forming a self-reinforcing cycle: real-world experience continually sharpens the world model, and a sharper world model in turn drives further policy improvement.

We term the world-model side of this cycle test-time physics grounding, a capability that hand-built physics simulators lack: while the world model serves as the training environment, real transitions from the policy it trains correct its dynamics through a lightweight LoRA pipeline.

Experiments on three challenging real-world tasks show that Rollback improves success rates over the strongest baseline by an absolute 10.67%, 11.11%, and 11.85% on block extraction, ball tossing, and tabletop curling, respectively, while achieving more stable improvement throughout training.

Although initialized from teleoperated demonstrations far below human level, Rollback surpasses the average success rate of human players on both ball tossing and tabletop curling within 8 hours of training.

summary.en: The paper presents Rollback, a method for improving robot policies with action-conditioned world models. It revisits key decision points, branches into alternative actions, and compares outcomes to create fine-grained action supervision without a separately learned value model. The system combines distributed model search with asynchronous real-robot execution, using real experience to update model dynamics. In three real-world tasks, the authors report gains over the strongest baseline and more stable training; on ball tossing and tabletop curling, the policy exceeds average human-player success rates within eight hours.
summary.zh: 论文提出 Rollback，一种利用动作条件世界模型改进机器人策略的方法：回到关键决策点，尝试替代动作并比较结果，据此形成细粒度动作监督，无需单独训练价值模型。系统将分布式模型搜索与真实机器人异步执行结合，用真实经验修正模型动力学。在三项真实世界任务中，作者报告其成功率较最强基线分别提高 10.67、11.11 和 11.85 个百分点，训练过程也更稳定；在投球和桌面冰壶任务中，训练 8 小时内超过人类玩家平均成功率。

items.title: Rollback: Experience Backtracking in World Models for Policy Improvement

sections.text:
Dexterous manipulation with multi-fingered hands is the next frontier of robotics, yet learned hand skills remain limited to simple grasps or basic repeated motions, such as rotating an object. As robots attempt more demanding in-hand maneuvers, safety, such as not dropping the object, becomes critical, yet it is rarely measured.

We study in-hand object pose reaching, a task that demands diverse and difficult grasps: moving an object to almost any position and orientation within reach of the fingers, at any wrist orientation, through long sequences of consecutive goals.

We present a recipe for training such policies for a LEAP hand in simulation without human data, built on a range of insights, from diverse resets and goals via generated grasp datasets to an adaptive friction curriculum.

With careful system identification, the policies transfer zero-shot to the real hand, using either motion capture or a single wrist-mounted depth camera, and prove remarkably capable and robust.

On top of the task policy, we add a learned residual safety filter with adjustable conservativeness, letting us tune the balance between performance and safety and greatly reduce object drops.

sections.text:
Humans are dexterous, but traditional data collection paradigms such as teleoperation, kinesthetic teaching, and wearable exoskeletons force humans to act through the robot embodiment, bottlenecking their dexterity. Retargeting can avoid this.

However, existing methods purely translate kinematics and ignore the real-world contact dynamics essential for task success. We present CARD: Contact-Anchored Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation, a simulator and object-free framework that retargets human demonstrations to robot actions by explicitly preserving contact force targets.

CARD unifies human data sources including video, motion capture, and tactile gloves via a shared hand--contact representation and generates explicit contact force targets in addition to kinematics. To maintain these contact targets during hardware open-loop replay, CARD also introduces a tactile tracking controller.

For video which does not contain an explicit tactile source, we present Vid-HACO, our video-to-contact model that sets a new state of the art.

Across our video, glove, motion-capture data and the GRAB dataset, CARD maintains contact on $43$--$78\%$ of contact frames, while kinematic and object-aware retargeting methods maintain contact on $ < 10\%$ and $22.5\%$ of the frames respectively.

Further, integrating our formulation into physics-based retargeting improves strict task success from 12\% to 32\% on GRAB dataset. Finally, we show that our tactile tracker is critical to reproduce demonstrated forces during hardware replay.

These results establish that contact preservation via CARD is a scalable interface for transferring human dexterity to robots.

summary.en: The paper introduces CARD, a framework that retargets human demonstrations to robot actions while preserving contact-force targets. It unifies video, motion-capture, and tactile-glove data through a shared hand-contact representation, and adds a tactile tracking controller for open-loop hardware replay. For video without tactile input, the authors present Vid-HACO to infer contact. Across several data sources and the GRAB dataset, they report contact preservation on more frames than kinematic and object-aware baselines. Integrating CARD into physics-based retargeting raises strict task success on GRAB from 12% to 32%.

sections.text:
Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models integrate high-level reasoning with low-level action execution for end-to-end robotic control. However, most VLA models target static manipulation in unconstrained environments, overlooking spatial constraints and dynamic obstacles.

Fine-tuning VLAs on obstacle-avoidance data is a straightforward solution, but collecting such data is costly, especially for dynamic scenarios, and may degrade their original task capabilities. To address these limitations, we propose VLA-Stem, a lightweight, reinforcement-learning-based safety mechanism for VLA systems.

Without fine-tuning the underlying VLA policy, VLA-Stem converts its action chunks into motion references and uses trajectory-level guidance to preserve their spatial intent while allowing flexible motion and timing adjustments.

Conditioned on these references, robot proprioception, and local obstacle information, the Stem policy adaptively modifies execution at inference time, preserving the original task intent while enabling responsive adaptation to spatial constraints and dynamic obstacles.

For robust and sample-efficient training, we combine teacher-student distillation with curriculum learning. We evaluate VLA-Stem on reference following, static spatial constraints, and dynamic obstacle avoidance.

Across six constrained simulation settings, VLA-Stem achieves 52.8% average collision-free task success versus 23.7% for the strongest safety baseline, while preserving base-policy performance in obstacle-free settings; real-world experiments further show consistent collision reductions under static and dynamic obstacles.

These results demonstrate that VLA-Stem couples high-level VLA task intent with rapid, reflex-like responses to immediate physical risks, providing a brainstem-inspired mechanism for robust robot execution.

summary.en: The paper introduces VLA-Stem, a lightweight reinforcement-learning safety mechanism that adjusts a vision-language-action model’s execution at inference time without fine-tuning its underlying policy. It uses action references, robot proprioception, and local obstacle information to adapt to spatial constraints and dynamic obstacles while preserving task intent. Across six constrained simulation settings, the authors report 52.8% average collision-free task success, compared with 23.7% for the strongest safety baseline. Real-world experiments show reduced collisions under static and dynamic obstacles.
summary.zh: 本文提出VLA-Stem，一种基于强化学习的轻量安全机制，可在推理时调整视觉语言动作模型的动作执行，而无需微调底层策略。它依据动作参考、机器人本体感知和局部障碍信息，在保持任务意图的同时适应空间约束与动态障碍。作者报告，在六种受限仿真设置中，平均无碰撞任务成功率为52.8%，高于最强安全基线的23.7%；真实实验显示静态和动态障碍下碰撞减少。

sections.text:
While velocity-commanded RL policies are effective for controlling quadrupeds, they are a limited interface for humanoids that need to perform complex whole-body motions.

Furthermore, RL tracking policies for whole-body motions typically have limited information about the desired future motion, preventing them from performing controlled deviations to achieve long-term task success; such information is particularly relevant when a controller must prepare for transitions between behaviors.

We address these challenges using concise motion representations that can be generated by a high-level controller, given a behavior label or text command. These representations can be fed directly into a tracking policy to provide a detailed motion reference.

Our method exhibits a high degree of flexibility in performing real-world robot motions such as dancing, fighting, or walking based on conditional information.

At matched capacity, our adopted stochastic motion tokenizer reconstructs motions from the Unitree G1 at a level that exceeds state-of-the-art approaches such as finite scalar quantization (FSQ) and the vector-quantized autoencoder (VQ-VAE).

The resulting discrete interface conditions whole-body tracking policies that execute generated dance, fight, and walk motions lasting 16.8 s each and a 35 s fight-to-dance sequence on a physical Unitree G1.

summary.en: The paper presents a stochastic motion tokenizer that compresses motions into representations generated from behavior labels or text commands and supplied to whole-body tracking policies as references. The authors report that the method supports conditional dancing, fighting, and walking by a humanoid. At matched capacity, it reconstructs Unitree G1 motions better than FSQ and VQ-VAE. A physical Unitree G1 executes dance, fight, and walk motions lasting 16.8 seconds each, plus a 35-second fight-to-dance sequence.
summary.zh: 论文提出随机运动标记器，将动作压缩为可由行为标签或文本指令生成的表示，并提供给全身动作跟踪策略作为运动参考。作者称，该方法支持人形机器人根据条件执行舞蹈、格斗和行走等动作；在相同模型容量下，其对 Unitree G1 动作的重建优于 FSQ 和 VQ-VAE。实体 Unitree G1 完成了各持续16.8秒的舞蹈、格斗和行走动作，以及持续35秒的格斗转舞蹈序列。

sections.text:
Vision--Language--Action (VLA) models generate robot actions from visual observations and language instructions, but their understanding of physical dynamics remains limited. Video world models can capture scene dynamics, yet generating future videos introduces high latency into the control loop.

We introduce PDRVLA, whose lightweight Physical Dynamics Module extracts physical tokens from vision--language features to condition action generation without online video generation. The module learns through direct prediction of future RGB, depth, and optical-flow features, with auxiliary supervision through a frozen pretrained video world model.

Training relies entirely on publicly available data, expanded through human-to-robot synthesis, subtask annotation, and embodied chain-of-thought (ECoT) annotation. Across four simulation benchmarks, PDRVLA achieves success rates of 99.3% on LIBERO, 89.9% on LIBERO-Plus, 93.6% on RoboTwin~2.0, and 81.5% on SimplerEnv.

Ablations show improved future prediction with world-model supervision and evaluate how subtask conditioning, future object-pose supervision, and ECoT training affect action success.

summary.en: PDRVLA uses a lightweight physical dynamics module to extract physical tokens from vision-language features and condition action generation without online video generation. The module learns by predicting future RGB, depth, and optical-flow features, with auxiliary supervision from a frozen pretrained video world model. Training uses only public data, expanded with human-to-robot synthesis and subtask and embodied chain-of-thought annotations. Across four simulation benchmarks, reported success rates are 99.3% on LIBERO, 89.9% on LIBERO-Plus, 93.6% on RoboTwin 2.0, and 81.5% on SimplerEnv. Ablations examine supervision and training components.

sections.text:
World Action Models (WAMs) learn representations for robot control by coupling future visual prediction with action generation. Successful manipulation depends primarily on how the robot and task-relevant objects evolve, whereas future-video prediction must also reconstruct the appearance and background of the entire scene.

We therefore propose Trace-WAM, which augments video-action learning with future 3D motion prediction as an auxiliary objective. This objective supervises temporal point correspondence together with image-plane displacement and depth change, directly describing the interaction dynamics and spatial changes involved in manipulation.

To this end, we adopt a three-branch Mixture-of-Transformer (Tri-MoT) architecture to jointly learn video prediction, motion prediction, and action generation. The motion expert predicts future trajectories from current visual features, allowing motion supervision to shape the representations used for action generation.

Because the action expert does not consume predicted trajectories, inference retains the current-observation policy path: a single visual forward pass followed by action denoising.

Experiments on RoboCasa-GR1, LIBERO, and LIBERO-Plus demonstrate strong in-distribution performance and out-of-distribution generalization, with particularly clear gains over Fast-WAM under limited demonstrations and distribution shifts.

summary.en: Trace-WAM adds future 3D motion prediction to video-action learning, supervising temporal point correspondence, image-plane displacement, and depth change to describe manipulation dynamics and spatial changes. Its three-branch Mixture-of-Transformer architecture jointly learns video prediction, motion prediction, and action generation. Since the action expert does not use predicted trajectories, inference follows a current-observation policy path. Experiments on RoboCasa-GR1, LIBERO, and LIBERO-Plus show, according to the authors, strong in-distribution performance and out-of-distribution generalization, with particularly clear gains over Fast-WAM under limited demonstrations and distribution shifts.
summary.zh: 论文提出 Trace-WAM，在视频—动作学习中增加未来三维运动预测目标，以监督时序点对应关系、图像平面位移和深度变化，描述操作中的交互动力学与空间变化。三分支 Mixture-of-Transformer 架构联合学习视频预测、运动预测和动作生成；动作专家不使用预测轨迹，因此推理仍采用当前观测策略路径。作者报告，该方法在 RoboCasa-GR1、LIBERO 和 LIBERO-Plus 实验中表现出较强的分布内性能和分布外泛化能力，并在示范有限及分布变化时尤其明显地优于 Fast-WAM。

sections.text:
Depth sensors are widely deployed across robotic platforms, and advances in fast, high-fidelity depth simulation have enabled robotic policies trained on depth observations to achieve robust sim-to-real transfer for a wide range of tasks.

Despite this, representation learning for depth modality remains underexplored compared to RGB, where large-scale foundation models now define the state of the art. To address this gap, we present DeFM, a self-supervised foundation model trained entirely on depth images for robotic applications.

Using a DINO-style self-distillation objective on a curated dataset of 60M depth images, DeFM learns geometric and semantic representations that generalize to diverse environments, tasks, and sensors. To retain metric awareness across multiple scales, we introduce a novel input normalization strategy.

We further distill DeFM into compact models suitable for resource-constrained robotic systems. When evaluated on depth-based classification, segmentation, navigation, locomotion, and manipulation benchmarks, DeFM achieves state-of-the-art performance and demonstrates strong generalization from simulation to real-world environments.

We release all our pretrained models, which can be adopted off-the-shelf for depth-based robotic learning without task-specific fine-tuning. Webpage: https://de-fm.github.io/

summary.en: DeFM is a self-supervised foundation model for robotics trained entirely on depth images. Using a DINO-style self-distillation objective on a curated dataset of 60 million depth images, it learns geometric and semantic representations; an input normalization strategy aims to retain metric awareness across scales. The authors also distill it into compact models for resource-constrained systems. On depth-based classification, segmentation, navigation, locomotion, and manipulation benchmarks, they report state-of-the-art performance and generalization from simulation to real environments. The abstract states that pretrained models can be used without task-specific fine-tuning.

sections.text:
Humanoids and other legged robots operating in complex environments must remember information that leaves their field of view and only becomes relevant much later. Reinforcement learning policies address this using memory networks such as LSTMs that are trained end-to-end with the policy to memorize such task-relevant aspects.

Yet, such architectures often fail to preserve sufficient information over long horizons. In this work, we propose a network architecture based on Hadamard memory that specifically targets robot navigation.

Our Local Spatial Matrix Memory (LSMM) enables RL agents to store generic task-relevant information at specific, position-based memory cells, enabling flexible and spatially grounded memorization.

We evaluate LSMM on the task of autonomous maze exploration, where it matches the maze coverage of strong recurrent and finite-history baselines while being the only architecture that remembers the maze layout, reducing the reconstruction error threefold.

summary.en: The paper proposes Local Spatial Matrix Memory (LSMM), a Hadamard-memory architecture for legged-robot navigation. It lets reinforcement-learning agents store task-relevant information in memory cells associated with specific positions. In autonomous maze exploration, the authors report coverage comparable to strong recurrent and finite-history baselines. Among the evaluated architectures, LSMM is the only one reported to remember the maze layout, and it reduces reconstruction error threefold.
summary.zh: 本文提出用于腿式机器人导航的局部空间矩阵记忆（LSMM），让强化学习智能体能在与位置关联的记忆单元中保存任务相关信息。作者在自主迷宫探索任务中评估该方法：其迷宫覆盖率与强循环网络及有限历史基线相当；在所比较的架构中，LSMM是唯一能记住迷宫布局的，并将布局重建误差降低至三分之一。

sections.text:
Accurate camera-LiDAR calibration is an essential prerequisite for robust multi-modal perception in robotics. Recent target-less methods based on learned pixel-point correspondences achieve high extrinsic calibration accuracy and generalize across environments.

However, they operate on rectified images with known camera intrinsics, restricting their applicability to systems whose cameras have already been individually calibrated. We present a fully automatic, target-less framework that jointly estimates camera intrinsics, radial-tangential distortion, and camera-LiDAR extrinsics from raw images and LiDAR scans.

Our method generalizes deep correspondence-based calibration from rectified images to raw cameras through intrinsic- and distortion-aware correspondence learning via synthetic augmentations. During calibration, we iteratively couple correspondence prediction and nonlinear optimization to jointly refine the camera parameters and relative sensor transformation.

We evaluate our approach on an unseen camera-LiDAR configuration from the KITTI dataset and on three real robotic platforms in a zero-shot manner.

The results demonstrate that joint calibration with our generalized pixel-point correspondence network improves extrinsic accuracy over correspondence-based methods using pre-calibrated cameras, while additionally recovering accurate intrinsics.

summary.en: The paper presents a target-less framework that jointly estimates camera intrinsics, radial-tangential distortion, and camera-LiDAR extrinsics from raw images and LiDAR scans. Synthetic augmentations support learning correspondences that account for intrinsics and distortion, while iterative prediction and nonlinear optimization refine the parameters and sensor transformation. The authors evaluate the method zero-shot on an unseen KITTI camera-LiDAR configuration and three real robotic platforms. They report improved extrinsic accuracy over correspondence-based methods using pre-calibrated cameras, along with accurate intrinsic recovery.

sections.text:
Humanoid parkour requires robots to reason about future footholds and whole-body motions over highly discontinuous terrain.

We revisit the information asymmetry in asymmetric actor-critic learning for perceptive humanoid locomotion: the critic exploits privileged simulator signals during training, whereas the deployable actor operates solely from onboard perception.

We argue that the key is not exposing privileged information to the actor, but learning a deployable approximation of it to narrow the information gap between training and deployment. We present HC2Robot, a deployable perceptive humanoid parkour framework consisting of a Predicted Foresight Module (PFM) and a Hyper-Connection (HC) Transformer.

PFM predicts from deployable observations the policy-conditioned timing, location, and support quality of each foot's next touchdown event, converting privileged supervision into a deployable latent representation that provides the actor with predicted touchdown information without privileged runtime sensing.

The HC Transformer further enhances temporal reasoning through learnable multi-stream routing, while a future motion prediction head provides short-horizon motion priors for regularization.

Across stairs, gaps, high platforms, and slopes, HC2Robot achieves a mean simulated traversal success rate of 97.60% and consistently higher safe foothold rates than strong perceptive locomotion baselines, supporting improved traversal performance and geometric foothold support under deployable sensing.

summary.en: The paper presents HC2Robot, a framework for humanoid parkour over varied terrain, combining a Predicted Foresight Module with a Hyper-Connection Transformer. From deployable observations, the module predicts the timing, location, and support quality of upcoming foot touchdowns, turning privileged supervision into a deployable latent representation. The transformer supports temporal reasoning, alongside a short-horizon motion prediction head. In simulations across stairs, gaps, high platforms, and slopes, the authors report a 97.60% mean traversal success rate and higher safe foothold rates than the compared perceptive locomotion baselines.

Vision-language-action (VLA) models provide a promising paradigm for scalable robotic manipulation, yet their reliance on success-only behavioral cloning leaves them brittle; lacking corrective training signals, minor execution errors rapidly compound into unrecoverable, out-of-distribution failures.

To address this limitation, we propose Adaptive Failure-Informed Learning (AFIL), an end-to-end framework that leverages failure trajectories as adaptive negative guidance for diffusion- and flow-based VLA policies.

AFIL uses a pretrained VLA to generate failure rollouts online, avoiding the need for handcrafted failure-mode design or human-in-the-loop recovery.

It then jointly trains Dual Action Generators (DAGs) for successful and failed behaviors while sharing a common vision-language backbone, enabling efficient failure-aware policy learning with limited parameter overhead.

During sampling, the failure generator adaptively steers action generation away from failure-prone regions and toward more reliable success modes, with guidance strength determined by the per-diffusion-step distance between success and failure distributions.

Experiments across in-domain and out-of-domain robotic manipulation tasks, covering both short- and long-horizon settings, show that AFIL consistently improves task success rates and robustness over existing VLA baselines, demonstrating its effectiveness, efficiency, and generality.

summary.en: The paper proposes Adaptive Failure-Informed Learning (AFIL) to address the brittleness of vision-language-action policies trained through success-only behavioral cloning. A pretrained model generates failure rollouts online, and success and failure action generators are trained jointly with a shared vision-language backbone. During sampling, the failure generator steers actions away from failure-prone regions, with guidance based on the distance between success and failure distributions at each diffusion step. Experiments on short- and long-horizon manipulation tasks, both in and outside the training domain, reportedly improve success rates and robustness over existing baselines.

The vision-language-action (VLA) and world-action model (WAM) communities debate whether control policies should inherit pretrained knowledge from vision-language models or from visual generators.

The debate, however, bundles three separable choices: backbone initialization, the objective applied to future observations, and whether the machinery for that future loss is kept at inference. A gap between a VLA and a WAM therefore cannot simply be attributed to any one of them.

We show that decoupling these choices yields a common framework for both families, which we term Just Action Model (JAM): a pretrained visual backbone with an action expert, trained with an action loss and a foresight loss.

The foresight loss trains current-observation features to predict frozen encodings of the recorded future through a prediction head discarded after training, so no visual generation is involved in either training or inference, and the backbone can be chosen freely.

We first compare objectives within fixed policy architectures, then evaluate the foresight recipe across backbone families. The resulting JAM policies outperform their matched FastWAM and ImageWAM counterparts on LIBERO and LIBERO-Plus, and achieve similar or slightly higher success rates on RoboTwin.

Compared with FastWAM, JAM improves the success rates from 97.0%/55.3%/91.2% to 98.2%/64.5%/91.4%, respectively. With cached foresight targets, JAM reduces estimated online training FLOPs per sample per update by 73% relative to FastWAM.

Our results show that future supervision improves control without visual generation or additional inference machinery, and strong foresight performance is attainable with either generator-initialized or vision-language backbones. Project Page: https://y0uroy.github.io/JAM

summary.en: The paper introduces Just Action Model (JAM), separating backbone initialization, future-observation objectives, and whether future-loss machinery remains at inference. JAM combines a pretrained visual backbone and an action expert, trained with action and foresight losses. The foresight objective predicts frozen encodings of recorded futures from current-observation features; its prediction head is discarded after training, so visual generation is not used. The authors report that JAM outperforms matched FastWAM and ImageWAM policies on LIBERO and LIBERO-Plus, and has similar or slightly higher success on RoboTwin. Cached foresight targets reduce estimated online training FLOPs per sample per update by 73% versus FastWAM.

sections.text:
This work investigates the use of event-based spiking controllers, implemented as spiking neural networks, for trajectory tracking in underactuated robots. Specifically, we address the problem of stabilizing a prescribed periodic orbit.

It is well known that, by applying the method of transverse linearization to the robot dynamics in a neighborhood of a periodic trajectory, the dynamics can be approximately described by a linear time-varying system with periodic coefficients (a periodic LTV system).

The problem of orbital stabilization can therefore be reduced to stabilizing the trivial solution of this LTV system. We show that a previously proposed Lyapunov-based greedy design, originally developed for LTI systems, can also be extended to the corresponding linearized transverse dynamics, which take the form of a periodic LTV system.

This enables the construction of a feedback controller for orbital stabilization of the robot. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated on the trajectory stabilization problem for the butterfly robot.

summary.en: This work studies event-based spiking neural network controllers for stabilizing prescribed periodic orbits in underactuated robots. Using transverse linearization near an orbit, the authors approximate the dynamics as a periodic linear time-varying system and reduce orbital stabilization to stabilizing its trivial solution. They extend a previously proposed Lyapunov-based greedy design for linear time-invariant systems to these transverse dynamics and construct a feedback controller. The method is demonstrated on a butterfly robot trajectory stabilization problem.

sections.text:
Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models remain brittle in long-horizon, contact-rich manipulation because success-only imitation provides little supervision for execution drift, while failed rollouts are often discarded.

We introduce RePO-VLA, a recovery-driven policy optimization framework that assigns distinct roles to success, recovery, and failure trajectories. RePO-VLA first applies Recovery-Aware Initialization (RAI), slicing each corrective suffix into a new episode so corrective actions depend on the current adverse state rather than the preceding failure.

It then learns a Progress-Aware Semantic Value Function (PAS-VF), aligning spatiotemporal trajectory features with instructions and successful references. The resulting labels salvage useful failure prefixes via reliability decay, while low-value labels mark drift and terminal breakdowns, teaching differences among nominal, failed, and corrective actions.

The data engine turns adverse states into planner-generated or human-collected corrective rollouts, teaching recovery to the success manifold. Value-Conditioned Refinement (VCR) trains the policy to prefer high-progress actions.

At deployment, a fixed high-value token biases actions toward the learned success manifold without online failure detectors or heuristic retries. We introduce the Failure-Recovery Benchmark (FRBench), with standardized error injection and recovery-focused evaluation.

Across simulated and real-world bimanual tasks, RePO-VLA improves robustness, raising adversarial success from 20% to 75% on average and up to 80% in scaled real-world trials. Code and video results are available at https://1018weijia.github.io/RePO-VLA-Web/.

summary.en: The authors introduce RePO-VLA to improve vision-language-action models in long-horizon, contact-rich manipulation. It assigns different roles to success, recovery, and failure trajectories, turns corrective suffixes into new episodes, and uses a progress-aware semantic value function to label trajectories and retain useful failure prefixes. Value-conditioned refinement trains the policy to prefer high-progress actions; deployment uses a fixed high-value token without online failure detectors or heuristic retries. The paper also introduces FRBench. The abstract reports average adversarial success rising from 20% to 75% across simulated and real bimanual tasks, and up to 80% in scaled real-world trials.
summary.zh: 本文提出 RePO-VLA，用于提升视觉—语言—动作模型在长时程、接触密集操作中的鲁棒性。框架分别利用成功、恢复和失败轨迹：将纠正动作片段切分为新回合，以当前不利状态为条件；通过进度感知语义价值函数标注轨迹，并保留失败前缀中的有用信息；再用价值条件精炼训练策略偏好高进展动作。部署时以固定高价值标记引导动作，无需在线失败检测器或启发式重试。作者还提出 FRBench。摘要报告，在仿真和真实双臂任务中，对抗成功率平均从20%提升至75%，规模化真实试验中最高达80%。

sections.text:
Spacecraft-mounted robotic manipulators can support long-term operability of orbiting assets by conducting tasks such as on-orbit assembly, repair, upgrade, and refueling.

In this context, the integration of continuum/soft robotic mechanisms into space manipulator designs promises to reduce stowage volume and mass, as well as to improve operational safety through the inherent mechanical compliance of soft structures.

This work presents a novel state reconstruction pipeline for a hybrid soft-rigid space manipulator, in which the distal link is a tendon-driven continuum robot.

The estimation problem is formulated as a maximum a posteriori (MAP) inference problem over the hybrid manipulator's configuration, conditioned on discrete, noisy measurements from joint encoders and a vision-based sensing pipeline.

The resulting soft-constrained optimization problem is transcribed as a factor graph, providing a compact representation for fusing heterogeneous measurements with the rigid-soft kinematic model.

Furthermore, the adoption of the Geometric Variable Strain (GVS) approach yields a minimum-order parameterization of the configuration, a property expected to facilitate model-based feedback control design in future work.

The proposed implementation is validated in simulation on a closed-loop trajectory where, for better realism, position measurements for the continuum link are obtained by means of a simulated visual pipeline leveraging synthetic photorealistic images.

The state reconstruction accuracy and computational performance confirm the potential of the proposed framework for hybrid soft-rigid robotic applications in orbit.

summary.en: This work presents a state reconstruction pipeline for a hybrid rigid-continuum space manipulator with a tendon-driven continuum distal link. It formulates estimation as maximum a posteriori inference from discrete, noisy joint-encoder and vision-based measurements, then represents the soft-constrained optimization as a factor graph that fuses measurements with the rigid-soft kinematic model. The Geometric Variable Strain approach provides a minimum-order configuration parameterization, which the authors expect may help future model-based feedback control. The implementation is validated in a closed-loop trajectory simulation, using a simulated vision pipeline based on synthetic photorealistic images for continuum-link position measurements.
summary.zh: 本文提出一种混合刚性—连续体空间机械臂的状态重建流程，其远端连杆为腱驱动连续体机器人。估计被表述为最大后验推断，依据关节编码器和视觉感知产生的离散噪声测量重建构型；软约束优化则转写为因子图，以融合异质测量与刚柔运动学模型。作者采用几何变量应变方法获得最小阶构型参数化，并认为这有望支持未来的基于模型反馈控制设计。实现通过闭环轨迹仿真验证，连续体连杆的位置测量来自合成照片级图像的模拟视觉流程；摘要称状态重建精度和计算性能显示了该框架的应用潜力。

sections.text:
Event cameras offer low latency, high dynamic range, and milliwatt-level power consumption, making them ideal for agile robots such as tiny drones navigating through cluttered environments. However, existing simulators generally render photorealistic images before converting them into events, making large-scale reinforcement learning prohibitively slow.

We propose an analytic event simulator that exploits what event cameras fundamentally measure - moving contrast edges - to synthesize event streams directly from scene geometry and ego-motion without visual rendering.

Our simulator generates a 64x64 event observation in 17 microseconds on a single GPU - over 400x faster than a state-of-the-art rendering pipeline - enabling end-to-end reinforcement learning for goal-directed obstacle avoidance to converge in under 30 minutes - three orders of magnitude faster than training on rendered events.

Policies transfer zero-shot to physically based event simulations (ray-traced Isaac Sim).Our policy reaches 83% success in cluttered courses unseen during training (mid-difficulty, traversability probability approx. 0.57), at 2.4 m/s average goal velocity, and retains 70% in a simulated texture-dense indoor hall.

Furthermore, we quantized the policy to a 1.2 MB int8 network running fully onboard a 56-gram Crazyflie equipped with a Prophesee GenX320 event camera and an OpenMV N6 microcontroller board.

Without any fine-tuning, external processing, or positioning, the policy achieves an average success rate of 82% (5/5, 5/6, 4/6 flights) across three real-world obstacle courses of increasing difficulty. Code: https://github.com/tudelft/rendering-free-event-nav

summary.en: The authors propose an analytic event simulator that generates event streams directly from scene geometry and robot motion, without rendering images, to speed reinforcement learning for autonomous navigation. They report generating a 64×64 event observation in 17 microseconds on one GPU, over 400 times faster than a rendering pipeline, and training obstacle avoidance to converge in under 30 minutes. Policies transfer zero-shot to physically based event simulations and are evaluated in unseen cluttered courses and a simulated texture-dense hall. The abstract also reports an average 82% success rate across three real-world obstacle courses with a quantized policy onboard a micro-drone, without fine-tuning, external processing, or positioning.
summary.zh: 本文提出一种无需图像渲染的解析事件模拟器，直接根据场景几何和机器人自身运动生成事件流，以加快自主导航强化学习。作者报告，单 GPU 生成64×64事件观测需17微秒，速度超过渲染流程400倍；避障训练可在30分钟内收敛，较基于渲染事件的训练快三个数量级。策略可零样本迁移至基于物理的事件仿真，并在训练未见的杂乱路线和模拟纹理密集室内场景中测试。摘要还报告，将量化策略部署于搭载事件相机的微型无人机后，在三个真实障碍路线中平均成功率为82%，未进行微调、外部处理或定位。

sections.text:
Legged robots for lunar exploration must be designed for low gravity, where reduced contact forces and long flight phases make leg morphology and controller choice interdependent.

We study this for a planar monoped in lunar gravity ($1.625$ m/s$^2$) using a bi-level co-design framework: a differential evolution outer loop searches over link lengths, and each candidate is evaluated on a vertical jump by either a quadratic program based task-space controller (QP-TSC) or a direct-collocation based trajectory optimization.

The two controllers yield different optimal link lengths, and trajectory optimization outperforms the QP-TSC across most of the design space, with 17% lower Cost of Transport (COT) at their respective optima.

We then extend to a 2D jump, where trajectory optimization with centroidal angular momentum regulation produces stable in-place and forward jumps, and an LQR controller absorbs impact and stabilizes the robot after touchdown. This is demonstrated on a baseline morphology with both links 0.3 m long.

summary.en: The paper studies morphology and controller co-design for a planar monoped in lunar gravity. Its bi-level framework searches link lengths and evaluates candidates using either a task-space quadratic-program controller or direct-collocation trajectory optimization. The authors report different optimal link lengths for the two controllers and better trajectory-optimization performance across most of the design space, with a 17% COT difference at their respective optima. For 2D jumps, centroidal angular-momentum regulation supports stable in-place and forward jumps, while an LQR controller stabilizes the robot after touchdown. The demonstration uses a baseline morphology with both links 0.3 m long.

sections.text:
Multi-arm manipulation has the potential to dramatically improve the throughput, efficiency, and dexterity of many manipulation tasks. Recent work coordinates multiple robot arms in a shared workcell by allocating and scheduling tasks for greater parallelism, jointly planning multi-arm motions, or directly learning multi-arm policies.

So far, these approaches are either too slow, rely on domain-specific assumptions, or scale poorly with the number of robots and task horizon.

Thus, we introduce cuArms, a conflict-based planner co-designed with GPU parallelism that efficiently decomposes the search space using reusable multi-modal roadmaps for individual robots and resolves conflicts and deadlocks through a lazy search.

To jointly optimize task assignment, schedules, motions, and manipulation skills, we integrate a high-level scheduler that proposes candidate skeletons for cuArms to ground into coordinated manipulation plans.

Experimental results show that our method establishes a new state of the art, with real-time initial solutions and anytime improvements in both motion quality and scheduling, without days of domain-specific training required by learning approaches. Videos of both simulated and real-world industrial tasks are available on https://cuarms.github.io/.

summary.en: The paper presents cuArms, a GPU-parallel conflict-based planner for multi-arm manipulation. It decomposes search using reusable multimodal roadmaps for individual robots and uses lazy search to resolve conflicts and deadlocks. A high-level scheduler proposes candidate task skeletons for the planner to ground into coordinated plans, jointly addressing assignment, scheduling, motions, and manipulation skills. The authors report real-time initial solutions and anytime improvements in motion quality and scheduling, without the lengthy domain-specific training they associate with learning approaches. The reported experiments cover simulated and real-world industrial tasks.

sections.text:
Vision-language-action (VLA) models increasingly run on edge devices aboard robots, where inference latency constrains closed-loop robot control. However, it remains unclear how to design VLA models, their inference software and edge hardware so that robots can run VLA inference in real time.

Most VLA models report only task success, while prior studies cover limited action-generation strategies, divide inference into at most three stages, and lack comparisons of inference optimizations on the same models.

Therefore, we introduce VLA-HWBench, a benchmark that measures 18 open VLA models on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor and AMD Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 395, with a seven-stage inference breakdown. Our study reveals three insights. First, action-generation strategy matters more than model size.

It dominates 14 of 19 Jetson configurations, latency varies by $82\times$ on Jetson and $157\times$ on AMD, and parameter count explains at most 15% of latency variance. Models that generate long action chunks in a few flow-matching steps keep up with control, whereas token-by-token decoding does not.

Second, kernel fusion with 4-bit weights helps most, running $\pi_{0.5}$ and GR00T N1.7 2.6-2.9$\times$ faster than PyTorch with torch.compile, but it exists for only these two models and only on the Jetson. Optimization also moves the time to the stages it shortens least, as CPU preprocessing grows from 12% to 39% of the GR00T N1.7 call.

Third, after optimization, memory bandwidth limits only the stages that process few tokens on the Jetson, such as the denoising steps, whereas software limits all other stages, from unfused kernels to serial preprocessing on the host CPU.

Overall, low-latency edge VLAs should use few action-generation iterations, inference software should extend kernel fusion and low-bit weights to more models and platforms, and edge hardware needs high memory bandwidth and a fast host CPU.

summary.en: The paper presents VLA-HWBench, which evaluates 18 open vision-language-action models on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor and AMD Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 395, with inference divided into seven stages. The authors report that action-generation strategy generally matters more to latency than model size: models generating long action chunks in few steps can keep up with control, while token-by-token decoding cannot. On Jetson, kernel fusion with 4-bit weights speeds up two models by 2.6–2.9×, after which software stages become bottlenecks.
summary.zh: 论文介绍 VLA-HWBench，用于评测 18 种开放视觉-语言-动作模型在 NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor 和 AMD Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 395 上的推理，并将过程拆分为七个阶段。作者报告，动作生成策略对延迟的影响通常大于模型规模；少步生成长动作块的模型可跟上控制，而逐 token 解码不行。Jetson 上对两种模型采用核融合和 4 位权重可加速 2.6–2.9 倍，但优化后瓶颈转向软件环节。作者据此提出扩展低比特权重与核融合，并重视高带宽内存和快速主机 CPU。

sections.text:
Electric vehicles (EV) create an urgent need for scalable battery recycling, yet disassembly of EV battery packs remains largely manual due to high design variability.

We present our Robotic Agentic Platform for Intelligent Disassembly (RAPID), designed to investigate perception-driven manipulation, flexible automation, and AI-assisted robot programming in realistic recycling scenarios.

The system integrates a gantry-mounted industrial manipulator, RGB-D perception, and an automated nut-running tool for fastener removal on a full-scale EV battery pack. An open-vocabulary object detection pipeline achieves 0.9757 mAP50, enabling reliable identification of screws, nuts, busbars, and other components.

We experimentally evaluate (n=204) three one-shot fastener removal strategies: taught-in poses (97% success rate, 24 min duration), one-shot vision execution (57%, 29 min), and visual servoing (83%, 36 min), comparing success rate and disassembly time for the battery's top cover fasteners.

To support flexible interaction, we introduce agentic AI specifications for robotic disassembly tasks, allowing LLM agents to translate high-level instructions into robot actions through structured tool interfaces and ROS services. We evaluate SmolAgents with GPT-4o-mini and Qwen 3.5 9B/4B on edge hardware.

Tool-based interfaces achieve 100% task completion, while automatic ROS service discovery shows 43.3% failure rates, highlighting the need for structured robot APIs for reliable LLM-driven control.

This open-source platform enables systematic investigation of human-robot collaboration, agentic robot programming, and increasingly autonomous disassembly workflows, providing a practical foundation for research toward scalable robotic battery recycling.

summary.en: The paper presents RAPID, a robotic platform for studying electric vehicle battery disassembly, combining a gantry-mounted manipulator, RGB-D perception, and an automated nut-running tool. It compares three fastener-removal strategies experimentally on the top-cover fasteners of a full-scale battery pack. The authors also explore translating high-level instructions into robot actions through structured tool interfaces and ROS services. In their evaluation, tool-based interfaces complete all tasks, while automatic ROS service discovery has a 43.3% failure rate.

sections.text:
Changing a deployment policy can invalidate a world model's uncertainty while leaving the physical transition mechanism and predictor unchanged. For one-step prediction, if source and target laws share the conditional mechanism $P(Y|X)=Q(Y|X)$, then the intervention is identified by the pre-outcome change of measure $w(X)=dQ_X/dP_X$.

For policy-controlled dynamics this ratio factors into state-occupancy and action-propensity terms. Weighted conformal calibration transports marginal coverage to the target law; with an estimated ratio $\hat w$, $P_Q\{Y \in C_{\hat w}(X)\} \ge 1-\alpha-TV(Q,\hat Q) \ge 1-\alpha-E_P|w-\hat w|$.

Population log-loss regret for a source-versus-target domain classifier bounds the same ratio error. If $h$ is its clipped target posterior, $\rho$ is the target-domain prior, and $\Delta(h)$ is population log-loss regret, then $E_P|w-\hat w_h| \le (1/(\rho\gamma))\sqrt{\Delta(h)/2}$.

An exact cancellation improves the dependence from a generic odds-map bound of order $\gamma^{-2}$ to $(\rho\gamma)^{-1}$.Our experiments use a released DINO-feature world model and physical Franka trajectories.

Under the strongest controlled state-action shift, ordinary 90% conformal sets cover 55.0%, whereas oracle and learned-ratio calibration cover 91.0% and 90.9%.The learned surrogate remains within 0.9% total variation of the target law. Calibration is relative to the deployment law: the model can remain fixed while calibration follows the intervention.

We machine-check in Lean 4 the finite-support algebraic and causal identities used in the classifier-regret argument, including its coverage-composition step.

summary.en: This paper studies uncertainty calibration for a fixed world model when the deployment policy changes. Assuming source and target laws share the conditional mechanism, the authors use pre-outcome change-of-measure weights for weighted conformal calibration and derive a bound linking classifier log-loss regret to weight error. Experiments use a released DINO-feature world model and physical Franka trajectories. Under the strongest controlled state-action shift, ordinary 90% conformal sets achieve 55.0% coverage, compared with 91.0% for oracle calibration and 90.9% for learned-ratio calibration. Some algebraic and causal identities are machine-checked in Lean 4.
summary.zh: 本文研究部署策略变化时固定世界模型的不确定性校准问题。在源与目标分布共享条件机制的前提下，作者用干预前协变量的变化权重进行加权保形校准，并推导分类器对数损失遗憾与权重误差的界。实验使用已发布的 DINO 特征世界模型和实体 Franka 轨迹；在最强的受控状态—动作偏移下，普通90%保形集合覆盖率为55.0%，基于真实权重和学习权重的校准覆盖率分别为91.0%和90.9%。部分代数与因果恒等式经 Lean 4 机器检查。

sections.text:
Failure diagnosers for robot manipulation are increasingly vision--language models (VLMs), trained and evaluated on single-arm failures produced by perturbing a successful demonstration.

Bimanual tool use adds failures of other kinds: a tool that slips out of its socket while still held, two correct gestures made at different times, and attempts that fail for two reasons at once. On a simulated bimanual tool-use task whose failure causes are read from the recorded trace, we measure what each sensing channel lets a diagnoser tell.

The tool's slip is read on the tool hand; which hand was late is read on both arms, while a sensor on one hand reads its own hand's delay and at most part of the other's; and whether a late attempt was also pushed too weakly is not identifiable from passive sensing when the tool hand is late.

Within two attempts, a repair policy that escalates when the cause is not identifiable repairs as many failures as one told the true cause. A VLM's internal state carries the late hand almost perfectly, along a direction no closer to the one its answer reads than a random one; whether the answer reports it depends on the wording of the question.

summary.en: This paper examines diagnosis and recovery for failures in simulated bimanual tool use, including tool slippage, mistimed gestures, and failures with multiple causes. Using failure causes recorded in the task trace, the authors assess what different sensing channels can identify. Slippage is observable on the tool hand, while identifying which hand was late requires observations of both arms. Passive sensing cannot distinguish a late attempt from one that was also too weak in a stated case. Within two attempts, a repair policy that escalates when the cause is unidentifiable repairs as many failures as a policy given the true cause. Whether a VLM reports its internal late-hand signal depends on question wording.
summary.zh: 本文考察双臂工具使用任务中的机器人失败诊断，关注工具滑脱、双手动作时序错位及多原因同时导致失败等情形。作者在仿真任务中依据记录轨迹中的失败原因，分析不同传感通道可识别的信息：工具手可感知滑脱，判断哪只手迟到需要观察双臂；被动感知无法在特定情况下区分迟到与推力不足。两次尝试内，遇到原因不可识别时升级处理的修复策略，修复失败数量与已知真实原因的策略相同。VLM 是否报告其内部表征的迟到手信息取决于问题措辞。

sections.text:
A robot policy needs to understand what a task is asking for in a scene, and how to move the robot to accomplish that task. To achieve these two skills, we introduce Zero-real Agent Policy (ZAP), a recipe that teaches a small off-the-shelf vision-language model to control a robot via a simple tool harness.

We use a pretrained 27B parameter model to bootstrap world understanding and reasoning, followed by supervised fine-tuning and GRPO on simple simulated tasks to teach it how to move the robot.

Without observing real-world robot data during training, ZAP reaches 96.7% success on real-world tasks, matching GPT-6 Astra in our harness and outperforming the MolmoAct2 VLA (33.3%), while running 3x faster and 17x cheaper than GPT-6 Astra.

Furthermore, ZAP also generalizes to an unseen embodiment as well as new objects, goals and strategies never seen during training. On a single-arm Franka, ZAP reaches 55.9% on RoboLab-120, 4.9 percentage points ahead of the leading VLA/WAM baseline.

sections.text:
Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) are laboratory systems that couple experimental planning, automated execution, and measurement feedback in a closed loop. Integrating flexible robot control with the typed application programming interfaces (APIs) and continuous measurements exposed by laboratory instruments remains an execution-interface challenge.

To address this challenge, we propose a traceable framework comprising four components: LAM (Lab Action Model), OpenSDL, Safe-SDL, and L3-Bench. LAM is a proposed measurement-conditioned policy architecture that extends vision-language-action paradigms to generate both continuous robot trajectories and typed instrument API calls.

OpenSDL is an execution substrate with an initial control implementation, designed to map role-level operations to heterogeneous devices, coordinate execution, and record timestamped causal events.

The proposed Safe-SDL runtime gate combines pre-dispatch schema and resource checks with signal temporal logic monitoring during execution, including extended waiting periods. L3-Bench (Level-3 Laboratory Benchmark) specifies an episode-level evaluation protocol covering physical outcomes, timing, reproducibility, safety violations, and fault recovery.

Together, these components provide an end-to-end design for linking hybrid action generation, monitored device execution, measurement feedback, and experimental evaluation, addressing coordination and traceability challenges in SDL workflows.

sections.text:
Robot foundation models may generalize across tasks and embodiments, but their actions still depend on sensors that can fail. When the policy is frozen or inaccessible, can an external monitor diagnose and repair corrupted inputs without access to its internals?

We test a structured surrogate that separates periodic gait from sensor-dependent corrections to guide input repair around a frozen locomotion policy. On simulated Go2, offline diagnosis raises walking success from 259/640 to 429/640 episodes; online repair reaches 382/640, with no triggers in 64 held-out fault-free episodes.

A matched boosted-tree surrogate predicts clean actions similarly well but yields no detected repair improvement over no repair. Separate fits improve walking on Go1 and ANYmal C, although phase-aware gradients perform better.

Evidence remains limited to one policy and a partly screened simulated fault suite; robot foundation model and hardware validation remain open.

summary.en: This study examines whether a structured, transparent surrogate can diagnose sensor faults and repair inputs when a robot policy is frozen or inaccessible. The surrogate separates periodic gait from sensor-dependent corrections. In simulated Go2 trials, offline diagnosis and online repair each improved walking success, while no repairs were triggered in held-out fault-free episodes. A matched boosted-tree surrogate predicted clean actions similarly but showed no detected repair benefit. Separate fits also improved walking on Go1 and ANYmal C, though phase-aware gradients performed better. Evidence is limited to one policy and a partly screened simulated fault suite; foundation-model and hardware validation remain open.

sections.text:
Humanoid behavior foundation models (BFMs) provide reusable whole-body motion priors: given a kinematic reference, they generate coordinated joint commands for motion replay, teleoperation, and VLA control.

However, trained primarily on flat-ground motion, BFMs lack an explicit mechanism to adapt foot placement, swing clearance, and contact timing to local terrain.

Many terrain-aware BFM approaches address this limitation by retraining or fine-tuning the tracker together with perception, incurring substantial data and computation costs while coupling ordinary tracking to the perception pathway. To bridge this gap, we propose GRAFT, a geometry-aware residual adaptation framework for frozen behavior trackers.

GRAFT preserves the BFM parameters and motion-reference interface, while a lightweight adapter adds terrain-conditioned corrections only to lower-body execution targets.

The adapter is trained with task and foot-geometry rewards, regularized to suppress unnecessary corrections on flat ground, and distilled from privileged terrain observations to onboard depth. Because the frozen BFM already provides whole-body reference tracking and nominal locomotion, GRAFT reduces terrain learning to a focused execution-adaptation problem.

We instantiate the framework on four frozen trackers and evaluate stairs, gaps, and platforms in simulation. We further validate it through real-world deployment on a Unitree G1, where the adapted SONIC tracker traverses terrain with onboard depth and unmodified references.

summary.en: The paper proposes GRAFT, a geometry-aware residual adaptation framework for frozen humanoid behavior trackers, addressing their limited adaptation to local terrain. It preserves the foundation model parameters and motion-reference interface while a lightweight adapter adds terrain-conditioned corrections to lower-body execution targets. Training uses task and foot-geometry rewards, suppresses unnecessary flat-ground corrections, and distills privileged terrain observations to onboard depth. The framework is evaluated in simulation on stairs, gaps, and platforms with four frozen trackers. The authors also report real-world deployment on a Unitree G1, where adapted SONIC traverses terrain using onboard depth and unchanged references.
summary.zh: 本文提出 GRAFT，一种面向冻结人形行为追踪器的几何感知残差适配框架，旨在补足其对局部地形适应的不足。框架保留基础模型参数和运动参考接口，由轻量适配器仅对下肢执行目标加入地形条件修正；训练结合任务与足部几何奖励，并抑制平地上的不必要修正。适配器通过特权地形观测训练并蒸馏至机载深度感知。研究在四种冻结追踪器上进行楼梯、间隙和平台的仿真评估，并报告 Unitree G1 实际部署验证：适配后的 SONIC 追踪器使用机载深度和未修改的参考轨迹通过地形。
