sections.text:
Running vision-language navigation fully onboard an aerial robot is hard, since grounding, planning, and control must share limited compute and a single-stage error is difficult to isolate in flight. End-to-end aerial policies fuse these stages into one network, giving up the observability and safety checks a modular stack keeps available.

We propose VLN on the Fly, an onboard stack that keeps grounding, planning, and control as separate, inspectable stages. A quantized VLM grounds an instruction to a coarse image cell, depth lifts it to a 3D goal, a fast B-spline planner returns a feasible trajectory, and a pretrained reinforcement learning policy tracks it to motor commands across quadrotors.

Across 15 onboard flights over three everyday referents in a controlled indoor volume, the stack reaches the target in 13 of 15 trials with 5.72 cm mean goal error and 39.3% average GPU utilization. In 6 additional cluttered-environment trials, the stack tracks collision-free trajectories under onboard perception gating.

summary.en: The paper presents VLN on the Fly, an onboard vision-language navigation stack that keeps grounding, planning, and control as inspectable stages. A quantized vision-language model maps instructions to coarse image regions; depth estimates a 3D goal, a B-spline planner produces a feasible trajectory, and a pretrained reinforcement learning policy tracks it to motor commands. In 15 onboard flights in a controlled indoor volume, the stack reached its target in 13 trials, with 5.72 cm mean goal error and 39.3% average GPU utilization. In six additional cluttered-environment trials, it tracked collision-free trajectories under onboard perception gating.

sections.text:
World action models (WAMs) have emerged as an important class of generalist robot policies, aiming to transfer video prediction priors to action learning. However, we find that existing WAMs frequently produce incorrect motion predictions in open-ended environment, leading to erroneous actions.

We attribute this limitation to two factors: （1） base video models are not optimized for manipulation, and （2） naively incorporating action components into video models can substantially degrade their generalization capabilities.

We introduce Video Prediction Policy 2 (VPP2), a WAM that enables strong zero-shot generalization in both video prediction and action generation. First, we curate a large-scale, diverse dataset of manipulation videos to continue pretraining the base video foundation model.

We annotate video clips with detailed captions and perform \textit{event-level} video pretraining to promote generalization across open-ended manipulation tasks. Second, we post-train and distill the video model into a single-step visual planner with fixed prediction horizon.

Finally, we introduce action module via a mixture-of-transformers (MoT) architecture to learn implicit inverse dynamics model.

Experiments demonstrate three key results: （1） VPP2-14B outperforms Cosmos3-64B by 11.0\% points in video prediction instruction-following success rate on open-ended tasks; （2） VPP2 surpasses the strongest baseline by 18.5\% points in success rate on real-world zero-shot ALOHA manipulation tasks; and （3） following benchmark-specific post-training, VPP2 achieves the highest success rates among evaluated methods on the challenging LIBERO-Pro, LIBERO-OOD, and RoboDojo benchmarks.

summary.en: The paper introduces Video Prediction Policy 2 (VPP2), addressing incorrect motion predictions by world action models in open-ended environments. The authors attribute the issue to base video models not being optimized for manipulation and to action components that may harm generalization. VPP2 continues pretraining on diverse manipulation videos with detailed captions and event-level training, then post-trains and distills the model into a single-step visual planner with a fixed horizon. A mixture-of-transformers action module learns implicit inverse dynamics. Experiments report gains in open-task video prediction instruction following, real-world zero-shot ALOHA manipulation, and several benchmarks after benchmark-specific post-training.

sections.text:
Long-horizon embodied navigation may be interrupted by a higher-priority instruction before the current task sequence is complete. The agent must finish its current atomic task, execute the inserted task, and resume the remaining sequence from the updated environment state, where its viewpoint and available navigation candidates may have changed.

To evaluate this capability, we introduce PIFR benchmark, a novel task for runtime task preemption and resumption in embodied navigation. PIFR includes single, repeated, and nested interruption settings,with stage-specific metrics for inserted-task completion, resumption of the original task, and completion of the full sequence.

Evaluations show that recovery performance varies across interruption conditions, while aggregate success can obscure differences in interruption handling and resumption. We further propose a lightweight candidate-ranking baseline to improve target re-grounding after interruption.

Together, PIFR and the baseline provide a systematic framework for studying interruption handling and task recovery in long-horizon embodied navigation.

summary.en: The paper introduces PIFR, a benchmark for evaluating whether embodied navigation agents can handle a higher-priority task inserted into a long task sequence and then resume the original sequence. It covers single, repeated, and nested interruptions, with separate metrics for inserted-task completion, resumption, and full-sequence completion. Evaluations show that recovery varies across interruption conditions and that aggregate success can conceal these differences. The authors also propose a lightweight candidate-ranking baseline for re-grounding targets after interruption.
summary.zh: 论文提出 PIFR 基准，用于评估具身导航中执行长序列任务时遭遇高优先级指令打断后，完成插入任务并恢复原序列的能力。基准涵盖单次、重复和嵌套打断，并分别衡量插入任务完成、原任务恢复和完整序列完成。评估显示，不同打断条件下的恢复表现有所差异，整体成功率可能掩盖处理打断及恢复任务的差别。作者还提出轻量级候选目标排序基线，以改善打断后的目标重新定位。

sections.text:
Robots that follow natural-language instructions unlock a wide range of autonomous applications in households, warehouses, and labs. Real-world environments are diverse and often heavily cluttered, requiring robots to plan over multiple steps, act, and replan as they work toward a goal.

We present CLARO (CLutter-Aware Robot Orchestrator), a VLM agent that orchestrates a set of perception and manipulation skills: open-vocabulary object detection, segmentation, 6-DoF grasping, and non-prehensile pushing to locate and retrieve a language-specified target in clutter.

CLARO maintains a memory of its past actions to support long-horizon execution, and emits manipulation targets (grasp poses/3D waypoints) allowing transfer across robot arms without task-specific training.

We evaluate CLARO against a range of methods on a dynamic simulation environment and standard image-based benchmarks, demonstrating strong generalization across object classes, lighting, and clutter levels. CLARO attains an average success rate of 89.1%, a relative improvement of over 16% on the strongest competing method in high cluttered scenes.

We further analyze performance along grounding and grasping axes to characterize where each method succeeds and fails. Finally, we deploy CLARO on a robot arm across diverse cluttered scenes, achieving a success rate of 88.8%, and demonstrating strong sim2real generalizability.

summary.en: The paper presents CLARO, a vision-language-model agent that coordinates perception and manipulation skills to find and retrieve language-specified objects in clutter. It combines open-vocabulary detection, segmentation, six-degree-of-freedom grasping, and pushing, while using action history to support long-horizon execution. Its grasp poses and 3D waypoints are intended to transfer across robot arms without task-specific training. The authors report evaluations in dynamic simulation, image-based benchmarks, and deployments on a robot arm across cluttered scenes.
summary.zh: 论文介绍 CLARO，一种使用视觉语言模型代理协调感知与操作技能的机器人系统，可在杂乱环境中根据语言指令定位并取回目标物体。系统组合开放词汇检测、分割、六自由度抓取和推挤，并利用过去动作记忆支持长时执行；输出抓取姿态或三维路点，以支持跨机械臂迁移。作者报告，CLARO 在动态仿真和图像基准上对物体类别、光照及杂乱程度具有较强泛化表现，并在真实机械臂的多种杂乱场景中进行了部署评估。

sections.text:
Human motion retargeting bridges the embodiment gap between humans and humanoid robots by converting human demonstrations into reference trajectories for whole-body control and loco-manipulation. For object-interaction tasks, successful execution depends on accurately preserving body--object relations at critical stages.

However, uniform per-frame iteration budgets do not account for these localized accuracy requirements, limiting the computational efficiency of retargeting. To address this limitation, we present Spatiotemporal Retargeting (STR), which uses keyframes and key body parts to allocate optimization effort.

Specifically, a vision-language model selects relevant motion signals and body parts, and keyframes are identified from changes in the selected signals. Based on these selections, STR assigns additional solver iterations to keyframes and higher interaction weights to the selected parts.

To further improve contact fidelity, we introduce Mechanics-Aware Contact Anchoring (MCA) to refine object-surface contact positions using an approximate object-wrench model while retaining the selected surface directions.

Building on the resulting references, we develop Spatiotemporal Reinforcement Learning (STRL), which combines adaptive key-stage sampling with a contact-position reward based on target proximity for downstream control.

Simulation experiments on a Unitree G1 and real-world experiments on a Unitree R1 demonstrate that STR improves geometric contact coverage and continuity at lower computational cost, while the resulting references improve downstream task completion across diverse object-interaction motions.

summary.en: The paper introduces Spatiotemporal Retargeting (STR), which allocates optimization effort using keyframes and selected body parts. A vision-language model selects motion signals and parts, guiding solver iterations and interaction weights. Mechanics-Aware Contact Anchoring refines contact positions using an approximate object-wrench model. The downstream STRL controller uses adaptive key-stage sampling and a target-proximity contact reward. The authors report simulation results on a Unitree G1 and real-world experiments on a Unitree R1, where STR improved geometric contact coverage and continuity at lower computational cost, and references improved task completion across object-interaction motions.
summary.zh: 论文提出时空重定向方法 STR，通过关键帧和关键身体部位分配优化计算量：视觉语言模型选择相关运动信号与身体部位，并据此确定关键帧、调整求解迭代和交互权重。为改善接触保真度，力学感知接触锚定方法 MCA 使用近似物体扳手模型细化接触位置。下游控制方法 STRL 结合自适应关键阶段采样和基于目标接近度的接触位置奖励。作者报告，在 Unitree G1 仿真及 Unitree R1 真实实验中，STR 以较低计算成本改善几何接触覆盖与连续性，生成的参考轨迹也提升了多种物体交互动作的任务完成情况。
